newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Cement shares lead trade on Nigerian bourse.
newsitem.headline: Cement shares lead trade on Nigerian bourse.

text.p: Cement companies were the best performers in active Wednesday trading on the Nigerian stock exchange, while food and oil marketing shares also rose.
The all-share index closed at 6,112.22 from 6,100.67 on Tuesday.
Cement Company of Northern Nigeria gained 10 kobo to 2.67 naira, while Ashaka Cement gained 10 kobo to 14.65 naira and West African Portland Cement gained 15 kobo to 27.25 naira.
In the oil marketing sector Mobil rose 12 kobo to 35.02 naira. National Oil closed up 10 kobo at 26.62 naira, Unipetrol rose the same margin to 33.20 naira.
The food sector saw moderate rises. Cadbury rose five kobo to 22.90, Flour Mills five kobo to 11.33 and Nigerian Bottling Company also closed five kobo higher at 25.80 naira.
Large volumes of packaging firms Carnaud Metal Box (CMB) and Delta Glass remained unsold, depressing prices by two kobo and three kobo, respectively, to 4.62 naira and 6.25 naira.
Metal products makers Vono finished at 2.34 naira, after adjusting for payment of 20 kobo dividend. ($1=80 naira)
